newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian coal said not in over supply.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian coal said not in over supply.

text.p: Moves by some Japanese utilities to call tenders for small proportions of their annual coal requirements recently does not mean excessive stock piles are being held by coal companies, Tony Haraldson, chief executive officer of Coal Operations Australia Ltd, said on Monday.
Haraldson told a coal conference that these tenders had been interpreted as an indication of an over-supplied market.
"My own feeling is that there is not an excessive of coal available and given clear loading ports, some suppliers may have difficulty meeting their offtake commitments," Haraldson said in a speech.
Haraldson said that the most recent tender, by Chubu Electric Co, called for 300,000 tonnes or five percent of the utilities annual coal requirements.
Haraldson said the timing of the tenders closing date of August 12 was deliberate, being seven months before the expiry of current full year prices already negotiated.
"Chubu wanted to insure that tender results could not be used in the next round of price negotiations," he said.
Haraldson said that Coal Operations Australia was one of 18 responding to the tender for the Chubu shipment.
"From our view point the existing contract coal was supplied in appreciation of and support for the long term existing business," he said. "The other coal was treated as a trial cargo".
He said the offers were not made because the company had excessive stock piles, "we do not," he said.
"They were made for strategic reasons and I believe other suppliers did like wise," Haraldson said.

Given recent disruptions at Australian coal mines and ports Haraldson said that it would be difficult to measure actual underlying industry stock piles that will exist when current commitments for deliveries are met.
Australia exported about 32.6 million tonnes of steaming coal to Japan in fiscal 1995 (April/March), Haraldson said, sighting statistics by Nissho Iwai Corp.
